checks.label: A logged axis puts each number at its log: 2, 5 and 20 sit 0.301, 0.699 and 1.301 of a × 10 space along, and on the ln axis 2, 5 and 10 sit at 0.693, 1.609 and 2.303

Only the right switches straighten each card: the gas and the lamp lie on a line with both axes logged and stay bent on every other setting; the capacitor's gap is bent on ordinary axes, lies on a line with only its y-axis logged, and bends again when t is logged too, dropping the 0 s reading

The gas line: handles on it at (0.301, 1.086) and (1, 0.176) give a gradient of −0.910 ÷ 0.699 ≈ −1.30, an intercept of 1.478 at log V = 0, and C = 10^1.478 ≈ 30, so 30 ÷ 4^1.3 ≈ 4.95 bar, beside the 5.0 bar read

RC is the time constant: the capacitor's ln(10 − v) line falls from 2.303 at 0 s to 0.182 at 100 s, a gradient of −0.0212 per second, which gives back RC ≈ 1 ÷ 0.0212 ≈ 47 s, and e^2.303 ≈ 10 V, the supply
Slope on a log-log graph is the exponent n: the lamp's readings, with both axes logged, lie on a line whose gradient is the power of d in its law, and that law gives back each reading
The special case n = 1 is the isothermal expansion: readings of pV = C, with both axes logged, lie on a line of gradient −1

Logarithmic graphs estimate the parameters of y = axⁿ and y = kbˣ from data for x and y: the gas gives its n and C, the capacitor its RC and supply, and the lamp its power and a, each only on its straightening switches

The intercept sits on the upright axis: at log x = 0, that is x = 1, on a logged x-axis, and at t = 0 on the capacitor's ordinary one; its tag says log C, ln a or log a, and a tick number beside it gives way
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture or lines gives it away, and a right answer shows it
Each puzzle offers three answers and takes only its right one, and every wrong answer has a hint of its own and draws its slip in red
A right answer to "which plot is straight" slides the capacitor's dots onto a line, and "not inverse-square" bends the lamp's
The drag maps the finger back to the same height: a finger at a handle sets it there, a finger off the top or bottom stops at the axis's end
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its time (3 to 4.5 s), none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
